papers.paper: B.Sc. Degree Examinations, Second Semester (CSC 584: ICT For Development)
Two ICT for Development questions on a page with no heading, filed with the 2024/25 second-semester papers

questions.text:
A regional development bank is preparing a funding proposal titled "Harnessing ICT for Inclusive Growth in West Africa." The lead consultant sends you a draft section that says: "ICT simply means computers and the internet. It is mainly used in business to process data faster. Most other communication tools like radio and television are no longer part of ICT."
1a. As an ICT specialist, critique this statement and provide a more accurate definition of ICT, drawing from accepted descriptions. (4 Marks)
1b. List six technologies (old and new) that should be recognised as part of ICT in the proposal. (6 Marks)
1c. Explain why education and digital literacy are critical to ICT-driven development in any country. (5 Marks)
1d. A government reports impressive ICT adoption in urban centres: high-speed broadband, smartphone penetration, e-commerce, and digital banking. However, rural communities still depend on basic phones and radio. Many schools there have no computers or internet. Explain digital divide using this scenario. (5 Marks)

A health startup wants to build a platform connecting urban doctors with rural patients for remote consultations, diagnosis and follow-up. They ask you to outline the ICT components required.
2a. Identify and briefly describe at least six ICT components (from the document) that will be necessary to implement this platform effectively. (6 Marks)
2b. Explain how the "application" of these components, not just their presence, creates both positive results and danger in such a system. Give 3 positive results and 3 dangers. (6 Marks)
2c. State 3 social development benefits this health platform could bring in a developing country context. (3 Marks)
2d. Your university launches a project called "Smart Campus 2030." The ICT Director says: "The project is purely an IT project – it is only about upgrading servers, installing Wi-Fi and developing new software. We don't need to involve telecommunications experts; this is strictly IT, not ICT." Differentiate clearly between ICT and IT, using this scenario to illustrate your answer. (5 Marks)

A Ministry of Education in a developing country wants to reduce travel costs for regional meetings with school principals across the country. They propose using teleconferencing instead of requiring everyone to come to the capital city.
3a. Explain what teleconferencing is, emphasizing its key features. (5 Marks)
3b. Discuss two advantages and one possible limitation of using teleconferencing for educational administration in a developing country. (3 Marks)
3c. A regional economic court in Africa is considering investing in tele-presence systems instead of standard video conferencing for cross-border hearings in commercial disputes. Explain what tele-presence is, in contrast to ordinary video conferencing. (4 Marks)
3d. Identify and describe four features that differentiate tele-presence from conventional video conferencing. (8 Marks)

A developing country wants to modernise its primary and secondary schools by integrating ICT into teaching and learning. However, many schools currently rely on chalkboards and printed textbooks only.
4a. Describe two ways in which ICT has transformed the educational process according to the unit. (5 Marks)
4b. Explain 5 ways how these changes can contribute to a better educational environment for learners. (5 Marks)
4c. Explain the following:
4c(i) Two impacts of ICT on industry. (2 Marks)
4c(ii) Two ways ICT has transformed entertainment and leisure activities. (2 Marks)
4c(iii) Describe two applications of ICT in home electronics. (2 Marks)
4d. Explain the importance of Big Data in ICT4D (4 Marks)

A Ministry of Planning in a developing country wants to launch a national big data initiative to improve evidence-based policymaking. An advisor says: "We need a systematic way to measure whether our big data plans fit our current reality. I heard about a 'Design–Reality Gap model', but I don't know what it is or how it works."
5a. Explain what is meant by Design Reality Gap in ICT4D. (5 Marks)
5b. Briefly describe how the Design–Reality Gap model works, with reference to big data initiatives. (5 Marks)
5c. Briefly explain the seven ITPOSMO dimensions used in the Design Reality Gap model. (7 Marks)
5d. Explain developmental informatics in the context of ICT4D. (3 Marks)

An international development agency wants to reduce the digital divide in remote communities. They plan to provide low-cost smartphones, train local ICT officers, and set up community internet hubs.
a. Explain the term digital divide using the scenario. (5 Marks)
b. Describe two developmental characteristics of ICTs that justify the agency's plan. (5 Marks)
c. Evaluate one advantage and one disadvantage of rapid ICT innovation for underserved communities. (5 Marks)

A major hospital network wants to implement an ICT-based healthcare system that includes electronic health records (EHRs), telemedicine, remote diagnosis, and global information sharing.
a. Explain how ICT can improve healthcare delivery in this scenario. (5 Marks)
b. Identify three ICT components that must be integrated into the hospital's system. (5 Marks)
c. Assess two possible online privacy and security risks involved in storing patient data digitally. (5 Marks)
